name: animoria-vscode
description: Visual Asset Governance for developers — discover, preview, trace, and clean up animated (Lottie, dotLottie, Rive, GIF, APNG, SVG) and static (SVG, PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF) assets directly inside VS Code.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No visual assets found in this workspace yet.

Animoria automatically discovers animated (Lottie, dotLottie, Rive, GIF, APNG, animated SVG) and static (SVG, PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF) files as you add them — no configuration needed.

Just added some? Indexing runs in the background and the Gallery updates on its own.

[Refresh Gallery](command:animoria.refresh)

animoria.enableThumbnails.markdownDescription: Generate static thumbnail previews for animated assets in the gallery sidebar. Rendered natively — no Chrome/Chromium installation required.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Animoria
walkthroughs.description: Discover, audit, and clean up the animated and static assets in your workspace.

steps.title: Visual asset discovery, built in
steps.description:
Animoria automatically finds Lottie, dotLottie, Rive, GIF, APNG, and animated SVG files anywhere in your workspace — and static SVG/PNG/JPEG/WebP/AVIF alongside them — and lists them in its sidebar. There is nothing to run and nothing to configure to start.

[Open the Animoria sidebar](command:animoria.gallery.focus)

steps.title: What gets scanned
steps.description: Every animated and static asset format Animoria recognizes is indexed automatically. Source files across common languages (TypeScript, JavaScript, Kotlin, Swift, Dart, and more) are scanned once, in a single pass, to find which assets your code actually references.

steps.title: Governance: rules you opt into
steps.description:
Governance is a set of configurable rules — unreferenced assets, byte-identical duplicates, oversized files, disallowed formats — that you enable in `.animoriarc`. Nothing is enforced until you say so.

[Run governance now](command:animoria.runGovernance)

steps.title: Reading a finding
steps.description: Every finding names the rule that produced it, the evidence behind it, and how confident Animoria is — evidence is never presented as more certain than the search that produced it. Findings also appear in the Problems panel (`F8` to jump between them).

steps.title: Resolving what you find
steps.description:
Review cleanup opportunities in one place before anything is deleted — nothing is removed without your confirmation, and deletions go through your editor's own undo history.

[Review cleanup opportunities](command:animoria.startCleanupReview)

steps.title: Configuring your own policy
steps.description: Add a `.animoriarc.json` at your workspace root to enable rules, with schema-backed completion as you type. Both `.animoriarc` and Animoria itself work with zero configuration if you never create one.
